summary: In Greek mythology, Aesepus (Ancient Greek Αἴσηπος) may name either the river-god son of Oceanus and Tethys who personifies the Troad river Aesepus, or — as in this atlas node — the Trojan warrior son of the naiad Abarbarea and Bucolion, twin of Pedasus, slain by Euryalus in Iliad 6.
etymology: Ancient Greek Αἴσηπος; also the name of the river (modern Gönen) and its town in the Troad.

sections.heading: Trojan twin of Pedasus
paragraphs: Homer's Aesepus and Pedasus are twins whom Abarbarea bore to Bucolion, Laomedon's illegitimate eldest son, while he shepherded. Mecisteus' son Euryalus strips their harness after killing Dresus and Opheltius — a brief Catalogue-of-the-slain vignette.

A separate Hesiodic Aesepus is the Oceanid river-god; some genealogies even make the nymph Abarbarea that river-god's daughter. The atlas id aesepus-trojan is the warrior twin alone, not the river personification.
